synopsis: A sleet-grey commuter line climbs onto a stone viaduct above the clouds and runs the length of halls the size of mountain ranges.

shots.prompt:
A completely ordinary world streams past the same left-side window in the dull light of a routine commute. Open on one arresting mundane detail passing close to the glass. By 2.5 seconds a two-note chime sounds and a calm neutral announcer says the destination line. Nobody reacts. Immediately afterwards the train accelerates hard and every body leans from inertia.

A sleet-grey suburban line in failing afternoon light: allotment fences, a football pitch, a supermarket car park sliding past the glass, bare trees and a chalk ridge standing far behind. The announcer says exactly: "Next stop: Valhalla."

Continuing from the previous final frame, the ordinary geography begins physically deforming toward the destination as the line climbs, descends, tunnels or crosses into weather. The world is still recognisably ours where the shot begins.

The line begins climbing hard. Cuttings give way to old stone embankments, sleet turns to dry snow streaking past the window, and the last farmhouse lights drop away below the level of the track as a bare white ridge already ahead keeps growing.

Continuing from the previous final frame, the train crosses the threshold layer. The last ordinary object grows, passes the window and recedes for the last time, and the passengers stop pretending this is a normal commute.

The train climbs onto a stone viaduct and crosses the cloud deck. The final pylon carrying the line grows, passes close and recedes behind into white. Above the cloud floor the light turns hard and low, and a dark shape stands on the horizon ahead.

Continuing from the previous final frame, the first true landmark of the destination resolves out of the far distance under the approach rule and continuously grows as the train closes on it.

The dark shape on the snow plain resolves into a hall the size of a mountain range, its roof shingled in overlapping golden shields, growing steadily across the window. Ravens cross the glass close and fast. Three more halls of the same size stand farther out on the plain.

Continuing from the previous final frame, the train races at close range alongside the destination's signature landmarks at maximum parallax, and the light of that place crosses the six fixed faces inside the carriage.

The train runs the length of the hall wall at close range. Barn-door-sized hammered gold shields pass one by one, firelight flashing between them across endless tables inside, and the six fixed faces catch the flicker. Beyond the receding wall the next hall is already growing.

Continuing from the previous final frame, travel alone carries the train into the heart of the destination. At about 9 seconds a calm ordinary commuter announcer quietly says the arrival line, then the dim destination board flickers to a new name that stays illegible, the chime sounds again, the voice begins only "Next stop—" and the shot ends mid-announcement while the train is still moving forward.

The train passes through the gate line into the hall field itself: firelit doorways, banners the height of the carriage, a mead lake, and roofs stretching to the snow horizon under a low burning sky. The announcer says exactly: "Welcome to Valhalla."
